sub_industry: 全国性股份制商业银行
current_cycle_state: Low-rate, low-NIM cycle. Sector valuation is mainly asset-quality and capital-return driven; PB remains the dominant anchor, with sustainable ROE and dividend yield explaining dispersion.

primary_anchor.method: PB adjusted by sustainable ROE and asset quality
primary_anchor.reason: Commercial banks are balance-sheet businesses. Book equity, asset quality, capital adequacy, and sustainable ROE are more stable valuation drivers than single-period earnings growth.

secondary_anchors.reason: In a low-rate environment, mature banks are also priced as cash-return assets; dividend yield is useful when payout is sustainable and capital ratios remain adequate.
Useful as a cross-check when earnings are stable, but should be normalized for credit cost, NIM pressure, and investment gains.
Useful for checking whether a premium to other joint-stock banks is supported by ROE, deposit franchise, and asset quality.

weak_or_floor_anchors.reason: A very low PB may reflect asset-quality concern rather than cheapness; use only after checking NPL migration, provision coverage, and capital adequacy.

disabled_anchors.reason: Bank cash flows are dominated by deposit, loan, and interbank balance-sheet movements and are not comparable to industrial free cash flow.
Bank growth is constrained by capital, risk appetite, NIM, and credit cost. High historical profit CAGR should not mechanically imply a growth-stock multiple.

anchor_switch_rationale: Use PB/ROE as the main anchor while NIM pressure, credit migration, and capital regulation dominate the sector. Increase dividend-yield weight when payout and capital adequacy are stable. Increase normalized PE only when credit cost and NIM are clearly normalized.
valid_when: the bank has positive book equity and normal regulatory-capital reporting
asset-quality metrics are available, including NPL ratio, provision coverage, and credit cost
sustainable ROE and capital adequacy can be estimated
invalid_when: asset quality is opaque or NPL recognition is suspected to lag
capital adequacy is near regulatory constraints or payout policy is unstable
major regulatory changes alter risk weights, capital rules, or deposit pricing before the next review
market_pricing_language: PB discount or premium versus sustainable ROE
key_cycle_indicators: NPL ratio and special-mention loan ratio
provision coverage and loan-loss reserve ratio
CET1 ratio and total capital adequacy ratio

analyst_notes: For high-quality joint-stock banks such as CMB, a PB premium over peers is acceptable only when supported by durable ROE, strong low-cost deposits, high provision coverage, and adequate CET1. Recheck after quarterly regulatory data or any major LPR/deposit-rate regime change.
